summary: Xinchuan Huang (1928–2021) specialized in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Peking University (~1953–1958) and served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences from around 1977 to 2000.

Xinru Liu (b. 1951) works in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history. She completed her PhD under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (~1980–1985), and held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences and The College of New Jersey.
Xiuzhi Zeng specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. Zeng completed an MA under Meihua Chen at Nanhua University (attested 2006).

Xu Dishan (1893–1941) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Yenching University, Columbia University, and the University of Oxford, and held posts at Peking University (~1927–1935), Tsinghua University (~1928–1930), and the University of Hong Kong (~1935–1941).

Xue Yu (b. 1964) specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He served as an assistant professor at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010), Visiting Professor of Buddhism at the University of Chicago (attested 2026), and Professor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Xuesong Zhang works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD at The Chinese University of Hong Kong under Xue Yu (attested 2008) and held a post at Renmin University of China (attested 2015).

Xuezhu Li is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who studied under Shoryu Katsura. Li was a Numata fellow at Ryukoku University in 2011 and a Research Associate at China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2010–2026).
Y. B. Damle studied under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held a post as Professor of Sociology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).
Yadi Qu works in Indology, Tibetology, and computational studies. Qu studied at and held a post as Wissenschaftliche Projektmitarbeiterin at the University of Hamburg (attested 2026).

Yael Bentor specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and Indiana University Bloomington (attested 1991), completing her doctorate under Gregory Schopen. She has held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (attested 1995–2000, 2026).

Yakupitiyage Karunadasa (1934–2026) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Ceylon and earned his PhD under David Friedman at SOAS/University of London (~1959–1963), later directing the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1991–2000).
Yanfei Zhou specializes in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology. Zhou earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under Yuet-Keung Lo.
Yang-Gyu An is a scholar of Buddhist studies. An studied under Hojin (attested 2003) and completed a D.Phil. at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich by 1998.
Yangdon Dhondup (b. 1970) works in the field of Tibetology. She completed her PhD at SOAS University of London under Henry Y. H. Zhao (~2000–2004).
Yanling Chen specializes in Buddhist studies. Chen studied under Hsing Yun and earned a Master of Arts under Yongdong Shi at Fo Guang University (attested 2012).

Yannick Laurent specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. Laurent holds posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a Wissenschaftlicher Mitarbeiter and at the University of Munich (both attested 2026).
Yanpei (1917–1996) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Taixu (~1934–1938) and Yinshun (~1941–1949).
Yao Wang (1928–2015) was a scholar in Tibetology and Sinology. He studied under Gongkar Tulku and served as a guest professor at the University of Vienna.
Yao-ming Tsai specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. Tsai completed a PhD at the University of California by 1997 and served as Professor of Philosophy at National Taiwan University.
Yaping Dou works in Buddhist and religious studies. Dou completed a PhD under Xue Yu at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
